text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today, but this came after a steep 8.6% slide over the past two weeks—a decline that tracks directly with crude oil prices falling sharply. Brent crude dropped below $90 a barrel on November 10th for the first time since August, driven by de-escalation talk around the Iran conflict; President Trump said he expected the war to end "fairly soon," which eased geopolitical risk and oil supply concerns. Since oil refiners and producers earn more when crude prices are higher, the drop from the mid-$100s to near $90 compressed valuations across the sector.

The modest bounce today may reflect some stabilization after the recent selloff, though the company still sits well below its November 3rd price of $144. The gap between US crude ($99.64) and world prices ($107.03) suggests tighter North American supply relative to global markets, which could be a mild tailwind for US-based producers—but not enough to offset the broader crude price weakness.
